page.layout: One block of text: a Latin verse poem in one column, with the closing initials "A. T. H." at the right and "FINIS" centred below. Page number 416 at the top. No running head, catchword or signature.

main_text.p:
Omnia complectens, nulli tamen ipse prebensus:
Omnibus infusus, labis at omnis inops:
Abripe me fursum, miro cum flamine mirus
Allabens lutea pectora fece laua:
Inq; tuam rape naturam, correptaq; flammis
Attenua, & formans attenuata joue.

Vnum sim tecum, maneam tibi semper adhaerens,
Numen idem ueluti cum genitore manes.

Plasma tuum instaura natiuo crimine fissum,
Assere & amissum uindice iure tibi:
Vt mea damna meo fatear tribuamq; furori,
Atq; accepta tibi commoda cuncta feram:
Qui mira bonitate malum conuertere nostrum
In tua letaris, Christe benigne, bona.

Pectoris ab hyemem, si non pietate calescat
Tam mira, & uero flagret amore tui.

Attonitum ab mentis somnum tristemq; ueternum,
Ni uigilet tantis illa agitata bonis.

Hoc opus haud nostrae: me Patris o alma voluptas
Christe mihi occidas, sic tibi uiuus agam:
Meq; mihi excidas, uiti quo palmes adorner
Florescamq; tibi, marcidus ipse mihi.

Incipiam nihil esse mihi: sic omnia abunde
Adueniant gremio suppeditata tuo.

page.notes: Several words are uncertain and should be checked against the scan: "prebensus" (possibly prehensus), "Allabens", "fursum" (printed long s, read as sursum/fursum), and "fece". The line "Pectoris ab hyemem" reads as printed. The poem's stanza division is not clear from the scan, so the couplets are grouped by sense and by the indentation pattern. No printing errors were corrected.
